finding.scope: Inspected official public server/task surfaces in exact C# SDK v2.2.0; no claim about private application-specific wrappers outside those surfaces.
finding.initial_execution: WithTasks is an alternate-result CallTool filter. For a task-backed call it durably calls IMcpTaskStore.CreateTaskAsync, captures the current request pipeline delegate `next`, then schedules Task.Run. The background body later invokes that captured `next`, which is why ordinary CallToolFilters run after task creation and before the matched tool on the original process.
finding.crash_boundary: A process crash after durable CreateTaskAsync but before or during volatile Task.Run destroys the captured `next` delegate. IMcpTaskStore persists task state/result/input requests but exposes no replay delegate, stored original request, claim-generation, or resume-existing-through-pipeline method.
finding.direct_primitive_negative: McpServerTool.InvokeAsync is a primitive tool invocation entrypoint. Calling it directly on restart is not equivalent to the ordinary CallTool request pipeline and does not by itself rerun CallToolFilters/current policy or authorization.
finding.fresh_request_negative: Re-entering through a fresh normal task-backed CallTool request reaches WithTasks again. IMcpTaskStore.CreateTaskAsync is specified to create a new task with a unique task ID, so stock v2.2.0 does not identify that fresh request as a resume of the already durable working task.
finding.internal_state_limit: ComposedCallToolInvocationState is internal and tracks in-process lifecycle coordination only; it is not a durable/public restart re-entry capability.
finding.missing_supported_seam: A safe stock restart path would need a supported entrypoint that accepts an already claimed durable task plus replayable original request/intent, skips only new-task creation, then rebuilds and executes the complete current ordinary CallTool policy/filter pipeline before the matched tool. No such public entrypoint was found in the exact v2.2.0 surfaces examined.
finding.external_effect_limit: Even such a seam plus a monotonic task-attempt generation would not by itself make arbitrary external effects exactly-once after lease expiry; the effect boundary still needs a stable idempotency identity or an atomic effect-side fence/CAS.

fixtures: initial task executes the ordinary policy pipeline
durable-create-before-schedule crash leaves a working task with no effect
direct primitive replay bypasses a revoked policy in the negative model
fresh normal retry creates a distinct task rather than resuming the existing one
hypothetical resume-existing seam reruns current policy and can block
monotonic claim generation can run one claimed existing task attempt
stale generation terminal write is rejected
attempt generation alone does not deduplicate an external effect already crossed
executed_artifact.execution_note: The source-equivalent harness was executed in the current Chat runtime before persistence; the persisted role-local artifact was then exact-read back. It models the documented/source ordering and entrypoint boundary rather than compiling the upstream C# SDK.
